thread:
maya: Customer reported a 400 from tool call when passing a Windows path with a caret in it. Pasting what they sent.
customer: Here is what I pasted into the tool args: 
```json
{"file_path": "C:\Users\alice\data^archive\report.json", "mode": "analyze"}
```
phil: hmm, caret (^) is special in cmd.exe — it escapes the next char. If they pasted that into a Windows shell command, it can mutate the string before it reaches our client.
maya: I pulled logs for req_0ab12 — parser error: `ParserError: unexpected control character at offset 22` right when we parse the JSON payload.
jordan: can you repro locally? Try running curl from Windows cmd vs powershell vs WSL.
maya: repro steps I ran (customer used cmd.exe):
```bash
# on Windows cmd.exe (what customer ran)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"file_reader","args": {"file_path": "C:\Users\alice\data^archive\report.json"}}'
```
jordan: yep that exact invocation will have cmd.exe process the `^` before curl ever sees it. On *nix the same string passes through fine which is why this didn't show up earlier.
support-bot: @channel Escalation created INC-35245 (P2) and attached logs.
maya: immediate workaround for customer: either run from PowerShell/WSL, or escape the caret by doubling it in cmd.exe (`^^`), or send args via a JSON file and `--data-binary @payload.json` so the shell doesn't interpret it. Example for cmd.exe: 
```bash
# escape caret in cmd.exe by doubling
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"tool\":\"file_reader\",\"args\":{\"file_path\":\"C:\\Users\\alice\\data^^archive\\report.json\"}}"
```
phil: created a short KB note we can link to customers about shell-escaping gotchas for tool args (windows cmd, powershell differences).
jordan: tagging @eng-infra to consider making our API layer validate raw bytes and reject if content-type mismatches or to document that we treat the request body as already-decoded JSON (we can't undo shell mangling).
maya: customer notified with workaround and KB link. They confirmed workaround worked in PowerShell. Closing loop unless eng wants deeper changes. :thumbsup:
